newsitem.title: ITALY: European assessment team leaves for Tirana.
newsitem.headline: European assessment team leaves for Tirana.

text.p: A high-level European assessment team left for Albania on Monday for talks on how to help the new broad-based government end the anarchy in the Balkan state, Italian military sources said.

The 11-strong team, led by Dutch roving ambassador Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg, took off for the capital Tirana by Italian military helicopter from the southern port of Brindisi after a preparatory meeting at the Foreign Ministry in Rome.
The team left from Brindisi in two Chinook helicopters at 1544 GMT, the commander of the Brindisi airbase said.

Diplomatic sources said the mission would first meet the ambassadors to Albania from the European Union and the United States before talks with Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and ministers in his broad-based unity government.

The sources said the mission was also expected to visit the ports of Durres and Vlore, key bridgeheads in any relief aid operation, during its two-day stay. No meeting with President Sali Berisha was immediately planned, they said.

EU foreign ministers declined at the weekend to answer an Albanian call for military intervention. The sources said the team would pave the way for a mission by up to 150 experts to help the Albanian authorities restore security and distribute aid.
